findings.where: First screen, Mark's large heading ('In my view, we are at a turning point in the story of public-private partnerships.')
findings.fault: The heading opens an argument that the page never finishes. It says there is a turning point but never says what it is, and nothing near the heading leads to the article where Mark makes the case. A visitor gets a teaser with no follow-up, and the line, though it is Mark's voice, says nothing about what he can do for them.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff weighing whether to hire an advisor. They will ask 'what turning point?', find no answer on the screen and no link to one, and have to work out his offer from the smaller paragraph underneath.

findings.where: First screen: the credential under the name ('Formerly Lead Lawyer, PPP Group, World Bank') and the rest of the hero
findings.fault: Nothing on the first screen shows that Mark is working now. His one credential is a former role, the heading comes from a 2020 blog post, and there is no recent talk, article, date or named piece of work next to the address. A first-time visitor can read 'formerly' as 'retired', and the page gives them nothing they can check.
findings.who_objects: A procurement-minded officer at a multilateral development bank. Before writing, they need to know he is active and has done this kind of work recently (first-visit trust items 3, 13 and 14, and 'the newest article or talk on the home page'), and the first screen shows only past standing.

findings.where: Phone, first screen: the yellow 'Write to me directly' strip above the 'I advise multilateral development banks…' paragraph
findings.fault: On a phone, the visitor is asked to write to Mark before being told what he does or who he works for. The only statement of his offer drops below the email strip and past the first screen, so the screen they see shows a face, a former title, an opinion and a request to get in touch.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who opens Mark's site on a phone from a LinkedIn link. They have no reason yet to write and must scroll past the call to action to learn whether he advises bodies like theirs.

findings.where: Article page specimen: the byline 'Mark Moseley · MMM Infra Blog No. 8 · 18 September 2024' and the end of the article
findings.fault: The article page has no one-line bio, no way home and no contact route. A reader who lands on the article from a social post sees only a name in small type and has no visible way to reach Mark when the piece persuades them.
findings.who_objects: A reader sent straight to the article from LinkedIn. Articles are where judgement is sold, and here, at the moment they are most convinced, they have no address and no idea who Mark is (first-visit trust items 7 and 12).
